supporting_news.title: Indian bonds breathe easy as Treasury yields decline
supporting_news.summary: Early Thursday, bonds issued by the Indian government saw slight upswings, influenced by a rally in US Treasuries. Despite this, concerns over liquidity, climbing interest rates, and mounting supply challenges have capped these hikes. Traders are curbing risk levels prior to a major debt auction, while rising domestic inflation fuels anticipations of a tougher monetary approach from the Reserve Bank of India, as evidenced by the expanding India-U.S. yield spread.

supporting_news.title: Yes Bank shares nosedive 20% after SC declares Rs 8,415 crore AT-1 bond write-off illegal
supporting_news.summary: In a pivotal decision, India's Supreme Court declared that the write-off of Yes Bank's 84 billion rupee AT-1 bonds is unlawful, causing a steep decline in Yes Bank shares. The ruling offers solace to bondholders, who successfully argued that their investments were misrepresented. This landmark decision raises critical questions about regulatory practices and bondholder rights, potentially reshaping market attitudes toward similar financial instruments.

supporting_news.summary: Sensex surged 1,534 points and Nifty gained nearly 375 points on Thursday, rebounding after the previous session’s decline. Gains in IT, banking and consumer stocks lifted sentiment. Falling oil prices and rupee strength also supported the market amid global volatility and concerns over US inflation.
